_comment: Copy to config.json and fill in YOUR OWN ids. Never commit real API keys — those live in your shell env or the connector, never in this file.

avatar._note: Generate ONE continuous master per reel. If your provider's vertical auto-crop misframes the face, generate 16:9 and crop with a measured face-x instead.
avatar._engine_note: ENGINE IS PER-LOOK, chosen by measurement — see avatarRegistry. Avatar V was locked on 2026-08-11, but the user's actual priority is GESTURES, and for the requested look (0aa05d6e, blue hoodie) Avatar V scores 0.48 (frozen) while avatar_iv + expressiveness:high + motionPrompt scores 6.01. expressiveness is avatar_iv ONLY (rejected on avatar_v) and motionPrompt needs a digital twin on avatar_v, which this group has none. So this look runs on avatar_iv. A look that gestures natively on avatar_v (48d4076, 5.32) keeps avatar_v. NEVER pick the engine by preference — measure.
avatar._speed_note: 1.12 + elevenlabs style 0.35 / stability 0.42 set 2026-08-25 on user note 'pace of the creator seems little slow and flat' about the 1.05 master; probed (fd83905a, ~3 credits) before the full regen — names, CTA and glossary all survive the pace. Supersedes the 2026-08-11 1.05 note. Send engine_settings {engine_type: elevenlabs, stability, style, similarity_boost: 0.85} with every generation.
avatar.motionPrompt: Confident tech presenter talking straight to camera, hands empty and visible. Gestures with open palms, counts points on fingers, lifts hands off the desk on emphasis, small forward lean on key numbers. IMPORTANT: hands hold nothing at any point - no pen, no phone, no papers, no props of any kind.
avatar._switching: Change presenter: `python3 tools/measure_avatar.py use <lookId>` (refuses anything measured frozen). Per-reel override: add "avatar": "<lookId>" to that reel's manifest.json.
avatar._motion_note:
VERIFIED 2026-08-12 by probe, not by assertion.
(#1) PROPS — FIXED. Probe be34b663 sampled every 0.4s (28 frames, hand region cropped): bare hands in every frame. The explicit prop ban works and stays verbatim in every motionPrompt.
(#7) EXPRESSION PER SECTION — IMPOSSIBLE ON A PHOTO AVATAR, and the sentence that used to sit in this prompt ('expression tracks the script rather than holding a fixed smile...') has been DELETED because it demonstrably did nothing. Evidence: with that sentence present the avatar grinned widest on the most serious line. expressiveness:low did not remove the smile either and dropped motion 6.90 -> 1.02 (stiff). A photo avatar is a deformation of ONE still image; this look's still is a smile, so no prompt can reach a neutral face.
WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS: pick the LOOK to match the reel's dominant register — avatarRegistry.register is 'warm' (0aa05d6e) or 'serious' (7123b3d0). One look per reel; the two looks have different wardrobe and background so cutting between them mid-reel reads as two different shoots.
IF true per-sentence expression is ever needed, that requires a DIGITAL TWIN driven by real footage. That is the one thing a twin genuinely buys — unlike the 2026-08-12 claim that a twin was needed for gestures, which measurement disproved.
avatar._render_note: 2026-08-13: `resolution` and `aspectRatio` were being left UNSET, so renders defaulted to 720p 16:9 and were then cropped+upscaled ~2.7x to 1080x1920. The API accepts resolution '4k'|'1080p'|'720p' and aspectRatio '9:16'. Digital twins are 4K-eligible; photo avatars never were. VERIFIED: aspectRatio 9:16 + resolution 1080p + fit cover renders NATIVE 1080x1920 with good framing — no crop, no upscale. USE IT for full-frame facecam beats. Keep generating 16:9 for `split` scenes, where the avatar occupies half the frame and the wider source is what you actually want. CAVEAT: both twin renders came back 25fps while the project is 30fps — conform on ingest; it is the render, not the source (preview is 30fps).
avatar._default_note: 2026-08-13: default switched from the photo avatar 0aa05d6e90e74f9fa23b75d0d8c267c4 to digital twin f55b0b7c at the user's instruction. WHY IT IS BETTER: motion 4.41 (gestures) vs the photo avatar's fixed-smile problem; the face stays LEVEL through a caveat, which no photo avatar can do at any expressiveness; native 1080x1920 output with no crop/upscale; same blue-hoodie studio so no wardrobe break with shipped reels. `expressiveness` was REMOVED because the API rejects it with avatar_v — it is Avatar IV + photo avatar only. The old photo avatars stay in avatarRegistry for reference and for any reel that specifically needs the WARM register, which this twin has not been proven to hold.
avatar._glossary_note: 2026-08-25: HeyGen brand glossary 'ai-reel-engine tool names' — ccusage -> 'see-see-usage', claude-hud -> 'Claude hudd'. The v1 claude-eating-tokens master spoke 'ccusage' as ~'accusate' (verified by whisper medium on the master AND fixed by probe 2c039525, ~3 credits). SEND brandGlossaryId ON EVERY GENERATION; pronunciations affect audio only, captions keep the written term. ADD new tool/product names to the glossary BEFORE generating, whenever the script contains a written-form name (lowercase CLI names, hyphenated repo names).
avatar._voice_note: MEASURED 2026-08-26. The cloned voice 'iGeeks Blog' (bb79e839) is the reason the read sounds flat, and no setting fixes it. Same text, same speed, TTS only: clone = 1.86 semitones of pitch movement (range 4.6); HeyGen stock voice 'Shaun' = 3.27 (range 10.6). Real creator references measure 3.74-6.63. Two avatar probes moving stability 0.42->0.28 and style 0.35->0.62, plus an eleven_v3 probe, changed NOTHING (2.02 and 2.74 vs 2.83 baseline) — a clone reproduces the expressiveness of its training audio, and cannot be argued into energy it never learned. THE FIX IS A RE-CLONE from expressive source recordings: see references/voice-clone-recording-spec.md. Do not spend more credits tuning stability/style against this clone.

faceFraming._note: Horizontal face-centre as a fraction of frame width. Measure it once per avatar on a mid frame (overlay a grid), save per reel to public/assets/<slug>/face-x.txt.

voiceClone._note: Optional. A clean ~18s sample of your own voice. Free community GPU space with a daily quota.

defaults._length_note: User rule 2026-08-11: every reel runs 1-2 MINUTES, picked from the topic. 2026-08-13 MEASURED delivery on this voice at speed 1.05 is ~2.7 words/sec (grok-bot 2.69, apple-pay-india 2.72, iphone18-split 2.55) — so 60s = ~162 words, 80s = ~216, 90s = ~243, 120s = ~324. Supersedes the unmeasured 3.2 wps figures; script_approval.py enforces the band at propose time.
defaults._caption_note: word-reveal is the production caption treatment (per-word reveal, emphasis list drives the accent keyword). Renamed 2026-08-16 from "nick-display"; the old name is still accepted for the seven reels already published.
defaults._style_note: Style ids describe the style, not its creator (renamed 2026-08-16): editorial = tech-news reporting, utility = tips/tools. Legacy ids varun / varun-mayya / nick / nick-saraev still resolve.

0aa05d6e90e74f9fa23b75d0d8c267c4._register_note: MEASURED 2026-08-12 (probe be34b663 + 5492c2c0). Source still is a smile ('Smiling podcaster in blue hoodie'), so every driven frame is a smile. Cannot carry a caveat, a warning or bad news at any expressiveness setting. Use for launches, features, positive reveals.

7123b3d03a3941538eac18fffc373aa8._register_note: MEASURED 2026-08-12 (probe 31699b25). Neutral source still -> level brows, no grin, mouth neutral except for speech, while still gesturing (2.97). This is the ONLY proven way to get a serious presenter. Wardrobe: grey sweater, blue/green desk studio — does NOT match the blue-hoodie look, so do not cut between the two inside one reel.

8e49c9d1b7f04fb0b454f86327f36a61.name: Dhvanesh -- 55 (digital twin #1)
8e49c9d1b7f04fb0b454f86327f36a61._register_note: MEASURED 2026-08-13 (probe 097841e1). GOOD NEWS: a digital twin BREAKS the fixed-smile problem — face stays level through the caveat, which no photo avatar can do at any expressiveness. BUT UNUSABLE FOR REELS: (1) 'iGeeksBlog' lower-third + social icons burned into 19/19 sampled frames plus a SUBSCRIBE button — trained on a PUBLISHED video, not raw footage; (2) 1280x640 @25fps, 2:1 aspect (source 1440x720) — a 9:16 crop off 640px height is 360x640 and needs ~3x upscale against our 1080x1920 @30fps; (3) head-and-shoulders framing puts the hands out of frame, so motion is 1.71 (stiff) and no motionPrompt can fix it. RETRAIN per references/digital-twin-recording-spec.md.

f55b0b7cb3b240298e9340a22d0265c2.name: Dhvanesh -- 59 (digital twin #2)
f55b0b7cb3b240298e9340a22d0265c2._register_note: MEASURED 2026-08-13 (probes d5006da2 + 768387f5). PASSES every source check that twin #1 failed: 16:9 30fps preview (not 2:1/25), NO burned-in branding (twin #1 had the iGeeksBlog lower-third in 19/19 frames), hands in frame and bare in 30/30 sampled frames, motion 4.41 (gestures) vs 1.71 (stiff). Face stays LEVEL through the caveat with no grin — the thing no photo avatar can do at any expressiveness. Same blue-hoodie studio as the shipped reels, so no wardrobe break. REGISTER: neutral-dominant. It does not grin through bad news, but it did not visibly warm up on the closing question either — treat it as a neutral/serious presenter, and do NOT claim a full warm-to-serious range until a probe proves one.

account._note: Upgraded to HeyGen Pro ($49/mo) on 2026-08-12: 436 premium credits vs ~134 on Creator. At ~1 credit per 3s of avatar, a 107s reel costs ~36 credits, so ~12 full reels per cycle. CONSEQUENCE FOR PLANNING: script changes are now affordable. Previously only footage/beat changes were free re-renders and a re-record was a real cost; now a bad script can simply be redone. Short A/B probes (~3 credits for 7s) should be used to verify prompt-side changes BEFORE committing to a full reel. NOTE: 4K output is gated on avatar TYPE, not plan — photo avatars cannot do 4K on any tier, so the old 'probe resolution 4k' item stays closed for this look.

voice._why: MEASURED 2026-08-27. The same cloned voice reads at 2.14 semitones through HeyGen's TTS and 3.60 through ElevenLabs v3 with audio tags — 0.998 speaker similarity, so it is the same voice, and 3.60 is the only reading this repo has ever measured above the 3.5 creator floor. Every HeyGen-side lever (eleven_v3 engine_settings, stability, audio tags in the script) moved it by 0.01, because uploaded audio bypasses TTS and script-embedded tags are stripped before the voice sees them. The variable was never the voice; it was who renders it.
voice._flow: vo_tagged.py -> creative_generate_speech (ElevenLabs MCP, eleven_v3, the voice id above) -> vo_external.py -> upload asset -> create_video_from_avatar with audioAssetId. HeyGen does LIP-SYNC ONLY. No manual step.
voice._guardrail: G53 — the whisper transcript of the uploaded audio must match the approved script at >=0.70. With TTS the audio was synthesised FROM the script and could not diverge; an uploaded file can, so the guarantee is now enforced rather than structural.
voice._fallback: Set mode to 'heygen-tts' to go back. avatar.voiceId and voiceSpeed are still correct for that path and are left in place deliberately.
voice._verified: 2026-08-27 via the connected ElevenLabs MCP: tags are ACTED not spoken (clean transcript), 3.17 semitones vs HeyGen's 2.14 on identical words (+48%), speaker similarity 0.991 against different-speaker controls at 0.959/0.964.
_known_limits: creative_generate_speech exposes NO stability parameter. The web UI does, and the user's hand-made 175s take hit 3.60 where this 9.6s take hit 3.17. Length, content range and stability all differ — untangle before assuming the API is worse.
A duplicate voice named 'Dhvanesh' exists (kjnHU2BEEUxL4teU1fAg). The id above is the one the user specified.
~190 credits per 9.6s => a 70s reel is roughly 1,400 credits.
